questions.question:
The diagram shows a shaded quadrilateral $P Q R S$ drawn on a grid. Each cell of the grid has sides of length $2 \mathrm{~cm}$. What is the area of quadrilateral $P Q R S$?
Choices:
A:$96 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$
B:$84 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$
C:$76 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$
D:$88 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$
E:$104 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}$

The heart and the arrow are in the positions shown in the figure. At the same time the heart and the arrow start moving. The arrow moves three places clockwise and then stops and the heart moves four places anticlockwise and then stops. They repeat the same routine over and over again. After how many routines will the heart and the arrow land in the same place as each other for the first time?
Choices:
A:7
B:8
C:9
D:10
E:It will never happen

The card shown is turned over about its lower edge and then about its right-hand edge, as indicated in the diagram.
Which view results?
Choices:
A:A
B:B
C:C
D:D
E:E

A large square is divided into smaller squares, as shown. What fraction of the large square is shaded grey?
Choices:
A:$\frac{2}{3}$
B:$\frac{2}{5}$
C:$\frac{4}{7}$
D:$\frac{4}{9}$
E:$\frac{5}{12}$

Which of the shapes below cannot be divided into two trapeziums by a single straight line?
Choices:
A:A
B:B
C:C
D:D
E:E

Four ribbons each have width $10 \mathrm{~cm}$. Each ribbon is $25 \mathrm{~cm}$ longer than the next smallest ribbon. The ribbons are then arranged to form two different shapes as shown in the diagram. How much longer is the perimeter of the second shape than the perimeter of the first shape?
Choices:
A:$75 \mathrm{~cm}$
B:$50 \mathrm{~cm}$
C:$25 \mathrm{~cm}$
D:$20 \mathrm{~cm}$
E:$0 \mathrm{~cm}$
Each of the designs shown is initially divided into squares. For how many of the designs is the total area of the shaded region equal to three-fifths of the area of the whole design?

The diagram shows squares of three different sizes arranged into a rectangle. The length of each side of the smallest squares is $20 \mathrm{~cm}$. What is the length of the marked path from $P$ to $Q$?
Choices:
A:$380 \mathrm{~cm}$
B:$400 \mathrm{~cm}$
C:$420 \mathrm{~cm}$
D:$440 \mathrm{~cm}$
E:$460 \mathrm{~cm}$
Each square in the grid shown is $1 \mathrm{~cm}$ by $1 \mathrm{~cm}$. What is the area of the shaded figure, in $\mathrm{cm}^{2}$?

A complete square is to be made using only pieces like the one shown in the diagram, without gaps or overlaps.
What is the smallest number of pieces required?

A regular octagon is folded exactly in half three times until a triangle is obtained. The bottom corner of the triangle is then cut off with a cut perpendicular to one side of the triangle as shown.
Which of the following will be seen when the triangle is unfolded?
Choices:
A:A
B:B
C:C
D:D
E:E

A rectangular sheet of paper which measures $6 \mathrm{~cm} \times 12 \mathrm{~cm}$ is folded along its diagonal (Diagram A). The shaded areas in Diagram B are then cut off and the paper is unfolded leaving the rhombus shown in Diagram C. What is the length of the side of the rhombus?
Choices:
A:$\frac{7}{2} \sqrt{5} \mathrm{~cm}$
B:$7.35 \mathrm{~cm}$
C:$7.5 \mathrm{~cm}$
D:$7.85 \mathrm{~cm}$
E:$8.1 \mathrm{~cm}$
In the diagram there are 7 squares. What is the difference between the number of triangles and the number of squares in the diagram?

The diagram shows an equilateral triangle RST and also the triangle $T U V$ obtained by rotating triangle $R S T$ about the point $T$. Angle $R T V=70^{\circ}$. What is angle $R S V$?
Choices:
A:$20^{\circ}$
B:$25^{\circ}$
C:$30^{\circ}$
D:$35^{\circ}$
E:$40^{\circ}$

The diagram shows a shape made from six squares, each measuring $1 \mathrm{~cm}$ by $1 \mathrm{~cm}$. The shape has perimeter of length $14 \mathrm{~cm}$. The zigzag shape is then continued until it has 2013 squares. What is the length, in $\mathrm{cm}$, of the perimeter of the new shape?

In the grid, each small square has side of length 1. What is the minimum distance from 'Start' to 'Finish' travelling only on edges or diagonals of the squares?
Choices:
A:$2 \sqrt{2}$
B:$\sqrt{10}+\sqrt{2}$
C:$2+2 \sqrt{2}$
D:$4 \sqrt{2}$
E:$6$

Which of the following diagrams shows the locus of the midpoint of the wheel when the wheel rolls along the zig-zag curve shown?
Choices:
A:A
B:B
C:C
D:D
E:E

A circle of radius 1 rolls along a straight line from the point $K$ to the point $L$, where $K L=11 \pi$. Which of the following pictures shows the correct appearance of the circle when it reaches $L$ ?
Choices:
A:A
B:B
C:C
D:D
E:E
The diagram shows a shape made from ten squares of side-length $1 \mathrm{~cm}$, joined edge to edge. What is the length of its perimeter, in centimetres?

Twelve congruent rectangles are placed together to make a rectangle $P Q R S$ as shown. What is the ratio $P Q: Q R$?
Choices:
A:$2: 3$
B:$3: 4$
C:$5: 6$
D:$7: 8$
E:$8: 9$
